Understanding pedagogical challenges faced by technology teachers in special needs classrooms
abstract: <jats:p>Teaching learners with special educational needs requires dynamic and adaptive pedagogical strategies that can lead to social development and academic success. This can be possible if teachers are assisted in mitigating the daily challenges of teaching such learners. This qualitative exploratory case study investigated the pedagogical challenges encountered by two Grade 9 Technology teachers in the Capricorn District of Limpopo Province. This study used Shulman’s Content and Pedagogical Knowledge framework to understand teachers’ challenges. Data was collected through semi-structured interviews and classroom observations; all collected data were analysed thematically. This study found that teachers experienced various challenges, including the emotional labour of teaching, burnout in the LSEN environment and the enactment of instructional knowledge. The study concluded that the sampled teachers displayed weaknesses in lesson planning, activating learners’ prior knowledge, diagnosing errors, achieving curriculum objectives and sustaining engagement. As a result, it was recommended that support through teacher assistants, creative differentiated strategies and enhanced digital-technology literacy to improve outcomes for learners with special needs was imminent.</jats:p>
venue: Journal of Education and Learning Technology

Integration of Biomechanics and Digital Technology: Using Kinovea for Motion Analysis and Learning for Beginner Athletes
abstract:
<jats:p>Background: The integration of biomechanics with digital motion-analysis technologies has introduced new approaches for examining movement efficiency, kinematic characteristics, and technical patterns in walking and running activities. Kinovea, as an accessible motion-analysis software, provides both visual and quantitative feedback. However, its application in supporting technique development among beginner athletes remains insufficiently explored.
Aim: This study aims to describe the use of Kinovea in biomechanics training and examine its contribution to the awareness of kinematic characteristics and movement techniques among beginner athletes.
Methods: A descriptive qualitative design involved 72 beginner athletes aged 18–25 years selected through purposive sampling. Data were collected over 16 weeks through interviews, field observations, and motion video recordings analyzed using Kinovea. Kinematic data focused on joint angles, stride behavior, and movement phases during walking, running, and the flight phase. Qualitative data were analyzed using content analysis with NVivo 12, while kinematic results were interpreted descriptively to identify performance patterns and areas for technical refinement.
Result: Kinematic analysis showed coordinated joint-angle patterns across all phases. Walking analysis identified arm swing angles of 50.9°–58.8° and leg separation angles of 64.3°–67.2°, indicating a stable gait rhythm. The running analysis revealed knee angles of 68.8°–69.8° and elbow angles of 87.6°–89.1°, indicating efficient propulsive mechanics. The flight phase demonstrated knee angles of 81.2°–87.8° and elbow angles of 80.4°–88.3°, suggesting effective momentum use and postural stability. These measurements supported stride-efficiency assessment and technique evaluation. Qualitative findings revealed that Kinovea enabled athletes to interpret movement phases and identify technical inefficiencies through slow-motion and frame-by-frame visualization.
Conclusion: Kinovea supports basic motion analysis by providing clear kinematic information and helping beginner athletes observe and refine their movement techniques. The findings also offer practical value for coaches by enabling more precise identification of inefficient patterns and guiding targeted corrections during early-stage training.</jats:p>
venue: Journal of Coaching and Sports Science

title: Sparsity Learning via Structured Functional Factor Augmentation
A Review of Phishing Detection Techniques Using Machine Learning and Natural Language Processing
abstract: <jats:p>The goal of phishing attacks, which rank high among cyber risks, is to steal sensitive information (such as login passwords, financial data, and more) from unsuspecting people and companies. Blacklist, whitelist, rule, heuristic, and signature-based detection methods are no longer suitable due to the rising sophistication of phishing schemes. As a result, ML, DL, and NLP are rapidly becoming into effective instruments for detecting both well-known and brand-new forms of phishing. Background on phishing assaults, old ways of detecting them, and recent advances in intelligent phishing detection are all included in this article. It delves into several machine learning algorithms such as decision tree, LSTM, ANN, CNN, and RNN, as well as deep learning models like KNN, NB, and SVM. Also, natural language processing methods including word embedding, sentiment analysis, text categorization, and tokenization are explored with the aim of detecting phishing material. Presenting a comprehensive, precise, and up-to-the-minute phishing detection system is the ultimate goal of this study, which focuses on machine learning frameworks, performance indicators, present obstacles, and future research directions.</jats:p>
venue: Journal of Global Research in Multidisciplinary Studies(JGRMS)

HYBRID NETWORK INTRUSION DETECTION SYSTEM BASED ON SIGNATURE ANALYSIS AND MACHINE LEARNING METHODS
abstract: <jats:p>In the context of increasing complexity of modern network infrastructures and the growing number of cyberattacks, improving the effectiveness of intrusion detection systems is a highly relevant task. The aim of this work is to develop and investigate a hybrid approach to network attack detection based on a combination of signature-based analysis and intelligent machine learning methods.  The research methods include analysis of requirements for anomaly detection systems, comparative analysis of existing solutions, design of a hybrid system architecture, and experimental modeling using multiclass classification of network traffic. The results demonstrate that integrating a neural model with a traditional detection system improves attack detection coverage and reduces the number of false positives.  The practical significance of the study lies in the possibility of deploying the proposed architecture in real corporate networks, while the theoretical significance consists in substantiating the effectiveness of a hybrid approach to traffic analysis. Future research directions include adaptive model training and expansion of the range of detectable attacks.</jats:p>

Unveiling the nine domains shaping occupational health literacy: A qualitative study.
abstract: BackgroundOccupational health literacy (OHL) refers to workers' ability to access, understand, appraise, and apply information to prevent work-related hazards and promote health at work. Despite its growing importance, there is no comprehensive, evidence-informed framework of determinants of OHL across multiple levels.ObjectiveThis study aimed to develop a multi-level framework of determinants of OHL by integrating findings from the literature with expert perspectives.MethodsThis qualitative study began with a targeted literature review using keywords related to occupational health literacy. From 455 records, 48 relevant studies were reviewed to identify factors influencing OHL and inform the interview guide. Second, semi-structured interviews were conducted with 11 purposively selected occupational health and safety experts (with at least a master's degree and five years of experience). Interviews continued until theoretical saturation was reached. Data were analyzed using thematic analysis guided by the constant comparative method, facilitated by MAXQDA software. A subset of transcripts was independently coded by two researchers; coding discrepancies were discussed and resolved, and codes were iteratively compared and grouped into categories and themes.ResultsThe analysis yielded 63 codes clustered into nine domains capturing determinants of OHL at individual, interpersonal, organizational, and policy levels. These domains encompassed personal and demographic characteristics, cognitive and practical skills, social and economic conditions, cultural and educational context, organizational policies and safety culture, work and environmental characteristics, and the content, communication, and enforcement of occupational safety and health regulations. Together, these domains describe OHL as the outcome of dynamic interactions between workers, their workplaces, and the wider regulatory and socio-economic environment.ConclusionThis study proposes an integrated, multi-level framework of determinants of OHL that moves beyond an individual-centric view and highlights the critical role of organizational and regulatory contexts. The framework can guide the development of measurement instruments and inform the design of multi-level interventions to improve OHL through changes in workplace practices, training strategies, and occupational safety and health policies.

title: Sleep and mental health outcomes following SARS-CoV-2 infection during pregnancy: A matched cross-sectional study.
abstract: This study aimed to compare sleep quality, mental health symptoms, and PASC outcomes among pregnant and non-pregnant participants with and without prior COVID-19 infection. A matched cross-sectional study design was undertaken, comparing four groups: 1) Not Pregnant, no prior COVID-19; 2) Not Pregnant, prior COVID-19; 3) Pregnant, no prior COVID-19; and 4) Pregnant and prior COVID-19. A total of 1,868 women were included in the analysis (934 pregnant and 934 not pregnant). Among participants with prior COVID-19, those who were pregnant had significantly more comorbidities, and higher hospitalization rates, compared to those not pregnant with prior COVID-19. Overall, prior COVID-19 infection was consistently associated with poorer sleep quality and more sleep disturbances, regardless of pregnancy status. In addition, participants who were pregnant with prior COVID-19 were more likely to report a shorter sleep duration of <5 and <6 hours per night, compared with those not pregnant with no prior COVID-19. Adjusted analyses showed pregnant participants with prior COVID-19 had worse sleep quality and more frequent sleep problems than non-pregnant participants without prior COVID-19. Furthermore, those who were pregnant with prior COVID-19 had a 1.76 to 2.69 times increased odds of developing PASC symptoms, compared to those not pregnant. These high rates of persistent PASC symptoms reported at 3 and 6 months, indicating more prolonged or delayed symptom expression. They also experienced worse mental health outcomes, with the prevalence ratio of having depression and anxiety symptoms occurring 1.89 and 1.72 times higher, respectively, among pregnant individuals with a history of COVID-19. Prior COVID-19 infection should be considered when assessing sleep and mental health in pregnancy due to its association with long-term PASC symptoms. Tailored post-COVID care, maternal health policies, and vaccination should be prioritized.
ai_summary: Study aimed to compare sleep quality, mental health symptoms, and PASC outcomes among pregnant and non-pregnant participants with and without prior COVID-19 infection . Participants who were pregnant had significantly more comorbidities, and higher hospitalization rates .

title: Artificial intelligence literacy among health-care professionals: a systematic review of reported competency needs.
abstract: Widespread calls for artificial intelligence (AI) literacy among health-care professionals have outpaced evidence on the AI information that should be taught and prioritised. We conducted a systematic review of studies published until Feb 12, 2026, following PRISMA 2020 guidelines (protocol preregistered on Open Science Framework). 70 studies comprising 42 empirical and 28 perspective or commentary papers from 21 countries were included after screening 4095 records. Among empirical studies, conceptual understanding of the meaning of AI (AI fundamentals; 88·1%), application of ethical thinking to AI use in clinical practice (ethical reasoning; 71·4%), and knowledge of existing AI tools (tools and applications; 71·4%) were the most prevalent competency domains. Perspective papers showed a similar pattern, with comparatively less emphasis on tools and applications. In 20 studies that asked students and health-care professionals to rank competencies by importance, tools and applications and the ability to evaluate AI before adoption (pre-adoption evaluation) ranked the highest. These findings inform a candidate foundation for the development of clinical AI competency.

title: Static and Dynamic Functional Connectivity Alterations of Medial and Lateral Entorhinal Cortex with Subjective Cognitive Decline.
abstract: Entorhinal cortex (EC), which is vulnerable in Alzheimer's disease (AD), comprises the medial (MEC) and lateral (LEC) regions encoding spatial navigation and olfactory information, respectively. However, it remains unclear whether static functional connectivity (sFC) and dynamic functional connectivity (dFC) of MEC and LEC are altered in subjective cognitive decline (SCD), a preclinical stage of AD, and how these changes relate to these functions. This study aims to explore the alterations in the sFC and dFC of LEC and MEC with the whole brain in the SCD population, and further to assess the relationships of these connectivity changes with olfactory and spatial navigation functions. We conducted neuropsychological evaluations, resting-state functional magnetic resonance imaging, spatial navigation, and olfactory assessment in 77 healthy controls (HCs) and 106 individuals with SCD. Bilateral MEC and LEC were defined as separate seed regions to calculate their sFC and dFC with all other voxels in the brain. Nested cross-validation classification analysis was applied to evaluate the classification efficacy for distinguishing SCD from HC. SCD individuals exhibited decreased sFC between MEC/LEC and widespread brain regions, primarily within the visual, sensory motor, and default mode network. The dFC between the left MEC and right putamen, and between the right MEC and right middle temporal gyrus increased, while decreased dFC was observed between the right LEC and right triangular part of inferior frontal gyrus. The connectivity between the LEC and visual network was significantly correlated with the olfactory recognition function. The predictive model combining sFC and dFC features from bilateral MEC and LEC achieved an area under the curve of 0.863. This study revealed that sFC and dFC alterations of MEC/LEC have occurred at the SCD stage, and these changes are correlated with spatial navigation and olfactory performance, demonstrating their potential as biomarkers for identifying individuals at risk for AD.

title: Enhanced Shallow-Feature Learning for Pediatric Renal Ultrasound Hydronephrosis Severity Classification.
abstract: Ultrasound severity grading of pediatric hydronephrosis guides whether a child receives surveillance, medical management or surgical referral, yet automated grading tools remain limited by single-vendor training, absence of external validation and unreported confidence reliability. This study develops and validates a four-class deep learning classifier (Healthy, Mild, Moderate, Severe) for pediatric renal ultrasound across multiple vendor systems, with external testing and confidence calibration analysis. Tailored to speckle-dominated ultrasound, the classifier, HarDNetE3, extends harmonic dense connectivity with three modifications (shallow-to-deep skip connections, squeeze-and-excitation recalibration, residual stabilization) to preserve the boundary and texture cues most diagnostic of pelvic dilation. A multi-vendor archive of 222,523 images was curated through a reproducible pipeline combining ICD code filtering, OCR and LLM measurement validation, posterior view restriction and region-of-interest cropping, yielding 14,231 images from 5383 patients across three vendor systems. On the held-out test set, the classifier achieved an F A multi-vendor, externally validated, calibration-aware classifier can grade pediatric hydronephrosis severity with clinically meaningful sensitivity and fewer high-confidence errors, supporting use as a decision-support tool alongside radiologist review. The underlying signal-informed design offers a transferable principle for other ultrasound classification tasks.

title: Quantitative Ultrasound-Based Machine Learning Versus the FAST Score for Identifying At-Risk MASH: A Retrospective Single-Center Study.
abstract: Since pharmacological therapies were approved for noncirrhotic adults with at-risk metabolic dysfunction-associated steatohepatitis (MASH), identifying this population noninvasively has become urgent. We therefore developed machine learning (ML) models using quantitative ultrasound (QUS) parameters and serum AST, and compared them with the FibroScan-AST (FAST) score. This retrospective study included 418 patients with biopsy-proven metabolic dysfunction-associated steatotic liver disease (MASLD), 138 with at-risk MASH. Five ML models were developed using four QUS parameters obtained from a general-purpose ultrasound system (LOGIQ E10, GE HealthCare) (ultrasound-guided attenuation parameter, integrated backscatter coefficient [IBSC], signal-to-noise ratio, and two-dimensional shear wave elastography), together with serum AST. Performance was assessed by nested cross-validation (CV) and compared with the FAST score using the DeLong test and Brier scores. A sensitivity analysis excluded patients with F4 fibrosis. SHapley Additive exPlanations (SHAP) quantified feature contributions. All five ML models outperformed the FAST score (cross-validated area under the receiver operating characteristic curve [CV-AUROC], 0.739 [95% CI: 0.690-0.789]; p < 0.05). Ensemble achieved the highest CV-AUROC (0.834 [0.795-0.873]), and the lowest Brier score (0.152). Results were similar after excluding F4 fibrosis (Ensemble, 0.827; FAST, 0.729; p = 0.001). SHAP identified IBSC as the most influential followed by two-dimensional shear wave elastography and AST. ML models integrating QUS parameters and AST outperformed the FAST score in identifying at-risk MASH in this single-center cohort, with Ensemble showing the best discrimination.

title: Spasmodic Dysphonia and Muscle Tension Dysphonia: A Review of Neuroimaging and Neurophysiological Evidence.
abstract: Spasmodic dysphonia (SD), or laryngeal dystonia (LD), and muscle tension dysphonia (MTD) are clinically overlapping voice disorders with different positions in current pathophysiological models. This review synthesizes multimodal neuroimaging and neurophysiological evidence on their central mechanisms, compares the implicated neural systems, and assesses whether such measures can aid future differential diagnosis. A structured search was conducted in PubMed/MEDLINE, Europe PMC, and Google Scholar (final search, March 29, 2026), limited to English-language publications from January 2000 through March 2026 and supplemented by reference-list screening and forward citation tracking. Evidence was synthesized across task-based and resting-state fMRI, structural MRI and morphometry, diffusion tensor and kurtosis imaging, PET, transcranial magnetic stimulation (TMS), and magnetoencephalography. Studies were appraised qualitatively for design, sample size, diagnostic phenotype, comparator groups, treatment or botulinum toxin washout status, findings, and limitations. The SD/LD literature provided relatively consistent evidence of abnormalities across distributed voice-control networks involving cortical, subcortical, cerebellar, and brainstem systems, recurring in primary sensorimotor cortex, supplementary and premotor regions, inferior frontal and parietal cortices, insula, putamen, thalamus, cerebellum, and their white-matter connections. Some abnormalities persisted outside phonation or before movement onset, supporting a trait-like component; TMS showed impaired cortical inhibition and a shortened cortical silent period (CSP) in SD/LD. The MTD evidence base remained limited, comprising one case-control task-fMRI study of ten women, one single-patient pre-/post-treatment fMRI study, and one TMS study with an MTD comparator. These findings suggested possible central involvement but did not establish a causal mechanism, a stable MTD-specific network, or the contributions of compensation, state-dependent effects, and phonatory effort; comparable CSP shortening was not reported in MTD. SD/LD is best understood as a distributed disorder of central voice-control networks, whereas MTD appears to be a hyperfunctional voice disorder with plausible but incompletely characterized central influences. Unequal evidence volume should not be read as established biological divergence, and the "neurological" versus "non-neurological" distinction remains provisional. Imaging and physiological measures are not yet validated biomarkers, and CSP is only a candidate marker pending replication and validation. Larger, clinically stratified, harmonized multimodal head-to-head studies are needed, potentially integrating neural, physiological, acoustic, and clinical measures for reliable differential diagnosis.
venue: Journal of voice : official journal of the Voice Foundation
ai_summary: Spasmodic dysphonia (SD), or laryngeal dystonia (LD) and muscle tension dysphonia are clinically overlapping voice disorders . This review synthesizes multimodal neuroimaging and neurophysiological evidence on their central mechanisms .

title: A dual-task prediction model for industrial equipment based on prior knowledge-enhanced shared features and dual-path gated recurrent units.
abstract: Remaining useful life (RUL) prediction and health state (HS) assessment are core tasks in industrial prognostics and health management. Most existing data-driven methods treat them as independent tasks, ignoring their inherent correlation and task specificity. A dual-task model based on prior knowledge-enhanced shared features and dual-path gated recurrent units (DP-GRU) is proposed. First, task-specific prior knowledge enhances shared spatio-temporal feature adaptability. Then, a dual-task output module is designed for task specificity. For RUL prediction, HS information adaptively evaluates RUL feature importance under different HSs, and DP-GRU boosts long-term memory for non-stationary data. For HS assessment, Additive Margin Softmax loss improves classification robustness. Finally, homoscedastic uncertainty optimizes dual-task loss weights. Three-case experiments verify its superiority over benchmarks and provide support for full-life-cycle equipment health management.
ai_summary: Remaining useful life (RUL) prediction and health state (HS) assessment are core tasks in industrial prognostics and health management .

title: Inactivation of the cGAS-STING-TBK1 pathway is associated with the progression from early melanoma to invasive melanoma.
abstract: Cyclic guanosine monophosphate-adenosine monophosphate synthase (cGAS)-stimulator of interferon genes (STING) signaling is a pivotal pathway to induce innate immune responses by detecting cytosolic DNA, which is released during tumorigenesis due to aberrant genomic events. A detailed examination to explore the activation of that signaling pathway in melanomas using clinical specimens has been limited to date. We tested the expression patterns of cGAS, STING and TANK binding kinase 1 (TBK1) phosphorylated at serine 172 (p-TBK1) in a variety of human primary melanomas to explore the activation of cGAS-STING signaling. Primary melanomas (60 patients) comprised of pTis (9 patients), pT1 (16 patients), pT2 (10 patients), pT3 (8 patients) and pT4 (17 patients) were examined using immunohistochemistry with antibodies against cGAS, STING and p-TBK1, and the expression levels of those proteins in melanoma cells were evaluated quantitively using an artificial intelligence assisted image analyzer HALO. Correlations with various clinical parameters and their prognostic significance were analyzed statistically and the diagnostic value of those were explored using ROC analysis. The expression of cGAS was significantly decreased in comparison between pTis-pT1 and pT2-pT4 (P = 0.000944). However, no significance in patient's prognosis was found. ROC analysis indicated that the cutoff value of cGAS expression with the highest discriminative power was at 0.9 mm with the area under the ROC curve (AUC) values of 0.78496. These findings show that the decreased expression of cGAS in melanoma cells has a significant impact on the progression from early melanoma to invasive melanoma.
ai_summary: Cyclic guanosine monophosphate-adenosine monphosphate synthase (cGAS) signaling is a pivotal pathway to induce innate immune responses by detecting cytosolic DNA, which is released during tumorigenesis due to aberrant genomic events .

title: Fractional order adaptive wavelet based neural network for system identification.
abstract: In this paper, a novel fractional-order adaptive wavelet neural network is proposed for the identification of fractional-order nonlinear systems. The proposed framework integrates three powerful tools-fractional calculus, dynamic neural networks, and wavelet activation functions-to achieve accurate system identification with fast convergence while avoiding an excessive increase in network complexity. By employing wavelets as activation functions, the proposed identifier is capable of capturing local features of the system. To reduce the required number of wavelets, their parameters are also updated in addition to the network weights using fractional-order adaptive laws defined in the sense of the Caputo fractional derivative. A fractional Lyapunov-based approach is utilized to derive the adaptation laws and to analyze the stability properties of the proposed identifier. It is shown that the identification error remains bounded even when the fractional order of the identifier differs from that of the target dynamical system. Moreover, sufficient conditions for asymptotic stability of the identification error dynamics are established by fractional-order extension of the classical Barbalat's lemma. To validate the proposed method, it is applied to the identification of oscillatory neuronal dynamics and a practical electromechanical system. Simulation results confirm that the proposed approach outperforms conventional fractional-order neural network identifiers in terms of accuracy, convergence rate, and network size.
